speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether there are adequate safeguards in place when the Police interview young suspects; and (b) whether the Ministry can provide an update on the review of the Appropriate Adult Scheme for Young Suspects (AAYS).

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The Police interview suspects to find out what happened.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It is not unusual that some suspects may be less than forthcoming during interviews.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Interviewers have to assess the situation and decide on the questions to be asked.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: It is accepted that young suspects may require more support during interviews.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Thus, as far as possible, the Police will interview young suspects in a Police station, away from their school or place of employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Should interviews need to be conducted at schools or places of employment, the Police will avoid drawing unnecessary attention or causing embarrassment to the young suspect.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: For instance, the Police may appear in plainclothes and use unmarked vehicles.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Ms Sun Xueling) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Thus, Appropriate Adults (AAs) will be activated for all suspects under 16.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am grateful to the Minister of State for the explanation.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Back in November 2021, I asked a Parliamentary Question on young suspects and the measures.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am heartened that the AAYS age threshold would be increased from 16 to 17, come October 2023.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I have a question on the limited pool of AAs and how we can perhaps increase it.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Would the Ministry consider, by default, having parents as AAs?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, AA would thus need to be an independent person.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We are definitely looking to increase the number of volunteers in the scheme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But where there are parents who want to volunteer as an AA to suspects who are not related to them, then, obviously, this is something that we would encourage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With regard to training, currently, the volunteers, the AAs, go through structured training.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They undergo a one-day training session which is conducted by the Singapore Children's Society.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And the training is supported by the Association of Criminal Lawyers of Singapore, the Law Society of Singapore and the Attorney General's Chambers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the point about whether or not we should involve PDO, currently, where the suspects are concerned, we use a pamphlet of rights to inform all suspects of their rights prior to interviews.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And the pamphlet is available to all Police stations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They are in very noticeable locations, in prominent areas, and this helps to standardise the way that suspects are informed of their rights during the investigation process.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Where suspects want to further obtain legal assistance or advice on their rights, this can be done through PDO or their own lawyers at various points of the investigation process, except that the lawyer will not be permitted to attend during the interview.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I would just like to assure the Member that there is structured training made available to volunteers, the AAs, and that the young suspects will have access to help should they require it during all points of investigation.
